extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, media scholars, journalism students and practitioners interested in constructive/solutions-focused reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing and assessing constructive journalism — a news approach that supplements traditional reporting with solution-focused, contextual, and future-oriented perspectives. Covers core elements, methods, expected audience effects, and cautions/limits for newsroom implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigates problems alongside responses and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism "investigates problems alongside responses and solutions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement traditional news reporting by including evidence-based responses and forward-looking angles; does not avoid critical reporting but expands it to cover how individuals, institutions, and communities address problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides context, nuance and multiple stakeholder perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should "provide context, nuance and multiple stakeholder perspectives."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden reporting beyond isolated incidents to include systemic context, diverse voices, and the societal implications of public problems to offer a fuller portrayal of conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporates forward-looking and explanatory questions (future orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive pieces "incorporate forward-looking and explanatory questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scenario and foresight questioning to explore long-term developments and implications; combine explanation with futures-oriented angles to help audiences understand trajectories and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlights progress, agency and evidence-backed initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism should "highlight progress, agency and evidence-backed initiatives."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise who is taking action, what measurable progress exists, and cite evidence for initiatives' effectiveness while avoiding overstating certainty or efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids sensationalism, distortion, and binary framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism "avoids sensationalism, distortion, and binary framing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist simplistic good-vs-evil narratives and sensational framings; maintain nuance and careful framing to prevent misrepresentation of issues or solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retains traditional journalistic values: accuracy, independence, verification and scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism "retains traditional journalistic values such as accuracy and independence, verification, and scrutiny."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain fact-checking, editorial independence and critical scrutiny even when reporting on solutions or hopeful developments to avoid advocacy or misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-element constructive journalism model
rubrics_metrics.description: A widely cited model identifies six core elements: "solutions, future orientation, context, inclusivity, empowerment, and co-creation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the six elements as an organising framework when designing stories or newsroom formats; ensure inclusivity and co-creation practices accompany solution and empowerment-oriented reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive interviewing using past- and future-oriented questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use "constructive interviewing" that employs past- and future-oriented questions (drawing on interventive questioning typologies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt questioning that explores what has been tried, what outcomes occurred, and what could happen next; influences include Karl Tomm's questioning typology and positive-psychology-informed approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions-focused research frameworks alongside problem investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine "solutions-focused research frameworks alongside problem investigation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design research that investigates root causes and simultaneously identifies, assesses, and contextualises responses; prioritize evidence and avoid superficial solutionism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-creation and participatory journalism (citizen dialogue formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ "co-creation and participatory journalism (for example, Room of Solutions formats)" and "citizen dialogue formats."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage communities and stakeholders in story development, use participatory methods to surface local responses and increase civic relevance and legitimacy of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual and data-informed storytelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support narratives with data and contextual analysis to help audiences understand scale, trends and systemic drivers; combine qualitative and quantitative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario and foresight questions about long-term developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate "scenario and foresight questions about long-term developments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply complexity theory and long-term scenario thinking to explore plausible futures, policy trade-offs and unintended consequences rather than simple prognoses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal 'solution tracking' in communities and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Undertake "longitudinal 'solution tracking' in communities and institutions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow initiatives over time to assess durability, scaling, unintended outcomes and actual impact; use longitudinal methods rather than one-off reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate audience effects: engagement, comprehension, trust, agency and news avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive approaches aim to "reduce news avoidance and support deeper comprehension", and to "improve audience engagement, trust and democratic participation" and "increase perceived self-efficacy and sense of agency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experimental and audience-research measures (engagement, recall, perceived usefulness, trust, self-efficacy, news avoidance) to evaluate impact; recognize effects vary by demographic, issue type, cultural context and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against normative or advocacy drift and blurring with strategic communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics warn of "risks of normative or advocacy drift if 'solutions' are framed uncritically" and possible "blurring of boundaries between journalism and strategic communication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure independence and critical distance when covering solutions; disclose conflicts of interest, scrutinise claims of effectiveness, and avoid acting as an uncritical promoter of particular interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for practical constraints: resource/time limits and breaking-news applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of "resource and time constraints in newsrooms, especially for daily hard news" and "challenges in adapting constructive methods to fast-paced breaking news coverage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt constructive methods pragmatically for newsroom workflows (e.g., integrate solution-context elements into short pieces, reserve deeper methods for enterprise reporting) and plan resources for longitudinal and participatory projects.
